title: Osero's upkeep obligation is binding while the mechanism for discharging it is left unspecified
content:
The Routine Protocol for the Ecosystem Upkeep Fee contains a single operative statement, A.6.1.1.7.2.3.1.2.1.2.1.1: "The process to pay 0.50% of Osero's market capitalization per year in USDS will be specified in future iterations of the Osero Artifact."

So the amount, base, currency and frequency are all settled while the mechanics are not. Unanswered questions include when market capitalization is measured (spot, average, at what date), the payment cadence, the destination, and what happens on non-payment — every question that determines whether a stated rate is enforceable.

The asymmetry is worth flagging rather than dismissing as drafting lag. The rate is the part that requires ecosystem-level agreement and is politically expensive to change; the mechanics are the part that can be settled operationally. Fixing the hard number first and deferring the plumbing lets the commitment bind immediately.

But it also means the Upkeep Rebate protocol, which depends on the fee payment as the moment of netting (A.6.1.1.7.2.3.2.2.1.2.1.2), is specified in more detail than the payment it attaches to. The dependent process is defined before the process it depends on.
description: The fee terms are fixed at 0.50% of market cap, but A.6.1.1.7.2.3.1.2.1.2.1.1 defers the actual payment process to future Artifact iterations.
